blogs.title: Turn LLMs into Feature Engineers: The Big Idea Behind FeatLLM
blogs.description: Instead of asking a large language model to predict every row, FeatLLM asks it to write human-readable rules that become new features. A simple downstream model then uses those features to make predictions. This shift cuts costs, speeds up inference, and boosts few-shot performance on tabular data.

blogs.title: Inside the Pipeline: How FeatLLM Turns Rules into Predictions
blogs.description: Walk through FeatLLM step by step: craft prompts with task and feature descriptions plus a few examples, guide the LLM through two-stage reasoning to extract class-specific rules, translate those rules into executable code, convert them into binary features, and train a lightweight linear model with non-negative weights. Finish with ensembling for stability and accuracy.

blogs.title: Faster, Cheaper Inference: No More Per-Row LLM Calls
blogs.description: FeatLLM only uses the LLM upfront to generate features, not at inference. That means production-time predictions are as fast and affordable as standard ML models, while keeping few-shot accuracy high. It works with API-only LLMs and avoids the need for fine-tuning or per-sample prompts.

blogs.title: Beating Prompt Limits on Wide Tables with Bagging and Ensembling
blogs.description: Long prompts break many LLM tabular methods. FeatLLM sidesteps this by bagging: it samples subsets of features and examples, generates multiple rule sets with controlled randomness, and ensembles the results. This handles 100+ columns, keeps prompts manageable, and improves robustness.

blogs.title: Interpretable by Design: Human-Readable Rules and Transparent Weights
blogs.description: FeatLLM outputs clear, domain-aligned rules that are turned into binary indicators. The simple model on top learns non-negative weights that show which rules matter most for each class. The result is an interpretable pipeline suited to regulated and high-stakes settings.

blogs.title: Less Fooled by Spurious Correlations in Few-Shot Settings
blogs.description: By separating general knowledge reasoning from example-based rule extraction, FeatLLM focuses on meaningful signals. Experiments show it degrades less than baselines when noisy, unrelated columns are added. Ensembling further filters out weak or misleading rules.

blogs.title: Prompting that Works: From Natural Language Rules to Executable Code
blogs.description: Learn the prompt design behind FeatLLM: basic information, two-step reasoning guidance, and strict response formatting to get usable, class-wise rules. Then see how the LLM is used again to translate those rules into simple Python for automatic feature generation, even with messy wording.

blogs.title: Do the Numbers Back It Up? Results Across 13 Tabular Datasets
blogs.description: FeatLLM outperforms recent LLM-based baselines like TabLLM and STUNT by about 10 percent on average and rivals classical ML that uses far more labeled data. With just a handful of examples, it delivers strong AUCs across diverse domains, including healthcare, finance, and synthetic tasks. Ablation studies confirm the value of tuning, reasoning guidance, and ensembling.
